questions.question: A transport model decides the number of trucks $t$ to hire, with $t\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$, and the litres of fuel $f\ge0$ to buy, a quantity that may be fractional. The objective and constraints are linear. How is this model classified?
options: A pure integer program, since one of its variables is integer
A linear program, since one of its variables is continuous
A mixed integer program, as only some of its variables are integer
Not an integer program, since not every variable is integer

questions.question: A production model has continuous output $x\ge0$ and a machine-purchase variable $y$ meant to be 1 if the machine is bought and 0 if not. The modeller writes only $0\le y\le1$, with linear objective and constraints. What does the model actually allow?
options: It is a MIP, because the bounds leave $y$ only the values 0 or 1
It is an LP in which $y=0.5$, half a machine, is feasible
It is an LP whose optimum always puts $y$ at 0 or 1 anyway
It is a MIP, because $y$ represents a yes-or-no decision

questions.question: A mixed integer program has integer variable $x_1\ge0$, continuous variable $x_2\ge0$ and linear constraints. Its integrality requirements are relaxed to obtain an easier problem that bounds the MIP optimum. Which problem results?
options: The same model with $x_1$ continuous and all constraints kept
The same model without $x_1\in\mathbb{Z}$ or the constraints with $x_2$
The same model with $x_2$ also restricted to integer values
The same model with $x_1$ continuous and free in sign

questions.question: A MIP has constraints $x_1+2x_2\le7$, $x_1\le3$, with $x_1$ a nonnegative integer and $x_2\ge0$ continuous. Which point $(x_1,x_2)$ is feasible?

A plant produces $x_1,x_2\ge0$ units (continuous) of two products under $x_1+x_2\le80+40y$, where $y\in\{0,1\}$ equals 1 if an extra machine is bought. A plan has $x_1=60$ and $x_2=45$. Which value of $y$ does this plan require?
options: $y=0$, since 105 does not exceed the capacity of $80+40=120$
$y=1$, since 105 exceeds the capacity of 80 left when $y=0$
$y=0$ or $y=1$, since the plan fits within the larger capacity
$y=0.625$, the value at which $80+40y$ equals exactly 105

questions.question: A MIP has constraints $x_1+2x_2\le8$ and $3x_1+2x_2\le12$, with $x_1$ a nonnegative integer and $x_2\ge0$ continuous. For $x_1=1$, which set of $x_2$ values is feasible?
options: All $x_2$ with $0\le x_2\le3.5$
Only the single value $x_2=3.5$
All $x_2$ with $0\le x_2\le4.5$

questions.question: A bakery model decides the number of ovens to rent $r$ (whole ovens), the kilograms of flour to buy $f$ (any amount) and whether to open a second shop $s$ (yes or no). Which domain declaration fits?
options: $r\ge0$, $f\ge0$ and $0\le s\le1$

questions.question: Continuous output $x\ge0$ must satisfy $x\le100+40y_1+60y_2$, where $y_1,y_2\in\{0,1\}$ indicate buying machine 1 or machine 2, and $y_1+y_2\le1$. What is the largest output any feasible plan can reach?

A maximization model with linear constraints is solved in three versions: with $x_1,x_2$ both integer (value $z_P$), with only $x_1$ integer (value $z_M$), and with no integrality (value $z_R$). Each version is feasible with a finite optimum. Which ordering always holds?
options: $z_P\le z_M\le z_R$, as each feasible set contains the previous one
$z_R\le z_M\le z_P$, as integer solutions are the most precise ones
$z_P\le z_R\le z_M$, as mixing variable types adds flexibility
$z_M\le z_P\le z_R$, as one continuous variable weakens the model

questions.question: A two-variable MIP has $x_1$ integer, $x_2$ continuous and a polygon of points satisfying its linear constraints. Why can its optimum not be found by evaluating the objective only at the corner points of this polygon?
options: Corner points are only defined for maximization, not for minimization models
All corners of the polygon are infeasible once $x_1$ is required to be integer
Corners may have fractional $x_1$; the optimum may lie mid-edge at integer $x_1$
The optimum of a MIP always lies strictly inside the polygon, not on its edges

questions.question: A maximization MIP has $x_1$ integer and $x_2$ continuous. After dropping $x_1\in\mathbb{Z}$, the relaxation's optimal solution is $(2.5,\,4)$ with value 20. Which conclusion about the MIP optimal value $z$ is justified by this information alone?
options: $z<20$, because the relaxation optimizer has a fractional $x_1$
$z$ equals the objective value at $(2,\,4)$ or at $(3,\,4)$
No feasible MIP solution exists, since $x_1=2.5$ is fractional
$z\le20$, and $z=20$ remains possible at another feasible point

questions.question: A minimization model with linear constraints has optimal value 40 when integrality is ignored and 46 when all variables must be integer. What can be concluded from these two values alone about the optimal value $z$ of the version where only some variables must be integer?
options: $40<z<46$ strictly

questions.question: A MIP maximizes $3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\le9$, $x_1\le4$, $x_1$ a nonnegative integer and $x_2\ge0$ continuous. What are its optimal solution and value?
options: $(4,\,2)$ with value 16
$(4,\,2.5)$ with value 17
$(4,\,3)$ with value 18
$(3,\,3)$ with value 15

questions.question: A firm earns 8 per unit of output $x\ge0$ (continuous), can sell at most 25 units, and pays a setup cost of 150 if it produces at all: maximize $8x-150y$ s.t. $x\le25$, $x\le40y$, $y\in\{0,1\}$. What is the optimal profit?

In a MIP, continuous output $x\ge0$ is linked to a binary setup variable $y$ by $x\le uy$, where $u>0$ is a constant chosen by the modeller and $y=1$ means production is set up. What must $u$ satisfy for the model to describe the situation correctly?
options: $u$ must equal 1, the largest value the binary variable $y$ can take
$u$ must be at most the smallest positive output a plan would use
$u$ may be any positive number, because $y=1$ switches production on
$u$ must be at least the largest output any feasible plan can have

questions.question: A plant's continuous output $x$ must be either 0 or between 20 and 50 units (a minimum batch if it runs at all). How can this requirement be written within a mixed integer program?
options: Add a binary $y$ with $20y\le x\le50y$
Impose $20\le x\le50$ together with $x\ge0$
Declare $x$ integer with $0\le x\le50$
Impose $x(x-20)\ge0$ together with $x\le50$

questions.question: A firm earns 5 per unit of continuous output $x\ge0$, can sell at most 140 units and has capacity $100+50y$, where $y\in\{0,1\}$ means buying a machine at fixed cost $F\ge0$. It maximizes $5x-Fy$ s.t. $x\le140$, $x\le100+50y$. For which costs $F$ is buying the machine ($y=1$) optimal?
options: Exactly when $F\le200$
Exactly when $F\le250$
Exactly when $F\le700$
Exactly when $F\le500$

questions.question: A MIP maximizes $4x_1+2x_2$ s.t. $x_1+x_2\le6$, $3x_1+x_2\le11.5$, $x_1$ a nonnegative integer, $x_2\ge0$ continuous. Without integrality the optimum is $(2.75,\,3.25)$ with value 17.5. What is the MIP optimum?
options: $(2,\,4)$ with value 16
$(3,\,2.5)$ with value 17
